ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is the primary coil of an ideal transformer. The primary side is connected in series with an ideal ammeter A1, and is connected to an AC power supply. On the right side is the secondary coil; the upper end of the secondary side is connected in series with an ideal ammeter A2 and then enters the light bulb network. In the figure, L2 is located in the lower loop of the secondary side, in series with the upper load part; L1 is the middle vertical branch; L3 is the right vertical branch, and the lower end of L3 is connected to the bottom node through switch S. Therefore, when S is closed, L1 and L3 are in parallel, and then in series with L2; when S is open, the L3 branch is open, leaving only L1 and L2 in series. Then reason: Let the resistances of the three identical bulbs all be R, and the effective voltage output by the secondary coil be U. When S is closed, the equivalent resistance of the secondary side is R + (R || R) = R + R/2 = 3R/2, so the A2 current is Ic = U/(3R/2) = 2U/(3R). When S is open, the equivalent resistance is R + R = 2R, so the A2 current is Io = U/(2R). The problem says that the A2 reading changes by 0.6 A, and after the switch is opened the load resistance becomes larger and the current decreases, so Ic - Io = 0.6, namely 2U/(3R) - U/(2R) = U/(6R) = 0.6, obtaining U/R = 3.6. An ideal transformer has no loss, and the change in input power on the primary side equals the change in output power on the secondary side. The effective value of the primary-side voltage is 18 V, and the A1 reading changes by 0.3 A, so the total power reduction is 18 × 0.3 = 5.4 W. The total power reduction on the secondary side also equals U(Ic - Io) = 0.6U, therefore 0.6U = 5.4, obtaining U = 9 V. From U/R = 3.6, get R = 2.5 Ω. Thus Ic = 2U/(3R) = 2 × 9/(3 × 2.5) = 2.4 A, Io = U/(2R) = 9/(5) = 1.8 A. L2 is connected in series in the main loop of the secondary side both when S is closed and when it is open, so the currents of L2 are respectively Ic and Io. The power reduction of L2 is R(Ic^2 - Io^2) = 2.5 × (2.4^2 - 1.8^2) = 2.5 × (5.76 - 3.24) = 6.3 W. 6.3 W is greater than 5.4 W.

method.method_draft: Let the secondary RMS voltage be U and each bulb resistance be R. From the circuit, with S closed, L1 and L3 are in parallel, so the equivalent load is R + R/2. Voltage division gives the voltage across L2 as 2U/3 and the voltage across each of L1 and L3 as U/3. With S open, only L1 remains in series with L2, so each has voltage U/2. The text says A1 decreases by 0.3 A while the primary RMS voltage is 18 V, so by ideal-transformer power conservation the total secondary power decrease is 18×0.3 = 5.4 W. Now compare the non-L2 bulbs: after opening, L3 loses U^2/(9R), but L1 increases from U^2/(9R) to U^2/(4R), an increase of 5U^2/(36R), which is larger than L3's lost power 4U^2/(36R). Hence the combined power of L1 and L3 actually increases by U^2/(36R) after S opens. Since the total circuit power still decreases by 5.4 W, L2 alone must decrease by 5.4 W plus this positive amount. Therefore the power decrease of L2 is greater than 5.4 W.

method.CoT_answer_check_final: 图像描述：电路图左侧是理想变压器原边，原边接 sinusoidal AC 电源，回路中串有电流表 A1。右侧副边上端经过电流表 A2 后到达上节点；上节点向下有灯泡 L1 连接到底部节点，右侧还有灯泡 L3 与开关 S 串联形成另一条从上节点到底部节点的支路；底部节点再通过灯泡 L2 回到副边下端。因此从图像结构看，S 闭合时，L1 与 L3 并联后再与 L2 串联；S 断开时，L3 支路被断开，只剩 L1 与 L2 串联。推理：设副边有效电压为 U，每个灯泡电阻均为 R。S 闭合时，L1 与 L3 并联等效为 R/2，再与 L2 串联，总等效电阻为 R + R/2 = 3R/2。分压得 L2 两端电压为 2U/3，L1 和 L3 各为 U/3。S 断开时，只有 L1 与 L2 串联，所以二者各分得 U/2。由于理想变压器且原边有效电压为 18 V，S 断开后 A1 读数减少 0.3 A，对应总输入功率、也即副边总功率减少 18 × 0.3 = 5.4 W。再看非 L2 灯泡的功率变化：L3 从 U^2/(9R) 变为 0，损失 U^2/(9R) = 4U^2/(36R)；L1 从 U^2/(9R) 增加到 U^2/(4R)，增加量为 5U^2/(36R)。所以 L1 与 L3 合计功率反而增加 U^2/(36R)。既然总功率仍减少 5.4 W，而 L1、L3 合计还增加了一个正量，那么 L2 的功率减少量必须等于 5.4 W 加上这个正量，因此大于 5.4 W。

raw_record.original_question: The figure shows a circuit containing an ideal transformer, with ideal ammeters in the circuit. The three light bulbs have identical and constant resistance. The primary coil of the transformer is connected to a sinusoidal AC voltage with an effective value of 18 V, and when switch \( S \) is closed, all the bulbs light up. After switch \( S \) is opened, the reading of ammeter \( A_1 \) changes by 0.3 A, and the reading of ammeter \( A_2 \) changes by 0.6 A. After switch \( S \) is opened, how does the power decrease of bulb \( L_2 \) compare with 5.4 W?
raw_record.answer: After switch \( S \) is opened, the power decrease of bulb \( L_2 \) is greater than 5.4 W
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is the primary coil of an ideal transformer. The primary side is connected in series with an ideal ammeter A1, and is connected to an AC power supply. On the right side is the secondary coil; the upper end of the secondary side is connected in series with an ideal ammeter A2 and then enters the light bulb network. In the figure, L2 is located in the lower loop of the secondary side, in series with the upper load part; L1 is the middle vertical branch; L3 is the right vertical branch, and the lower end of L3 is connected to the bottom node through switch S. Therefore, when S is closed, L1 and L3 are in parallel, and then in series with L2; when S is open, the L3 branch is open, leaving only L1 and L2 in series.

Then reason: Let the resistances of the three identical bulbs all be R, and the effective voltage output by the secondary coil be U. When S is closed, the equivalent resistance of the secondary side is R + (R || R) = R + R/2 = 3R/2, so the A2 current is Ic = U/(3R/2) = 2U/(3R). When S is open, the equivalent resistance is R + R = 2R, so the A2 current is Io = U/(2R). The problem says that the A2 reading changes by 0.6 A, and after the switch is opened the load resistance becomes larger and the current decreases, so Ic - Io = 0.6, namely 2U/(3R) - U/(2R) = U/(6R) = 0.6, obtaining U/R = 3.6.

An ideal transformer has no loss, and the change in input power on the primary side equals the change in output power on the secondary side. The effective value of the primary-side voltage is 18 V, and the A1 reading changes by 0.3 A, so the total power reduction is 18 × 0.3 = 5.4 W. The total power reduction on the secondary side also equals U(Ic - Io) = 0.6U, therefore 0.6U = 5.4, obtaining U = 9 V. From U/R = 3.6, get R = 2.5 Ω.

Thus Ic = 2U/(3R) = 2 × 9/(3 × 2.5) = 2.4 A, Io = U/(2R) = 9/(5) = 1.8 A. L2 is connected in series in the main loop of the secondary side both when S is closed and when it is open, so the currents of L2 are respectively Ic and Io. The power reduction of L2 is R(Ic^2 - Io^2) = 2.5 × (2.4^2 - 1.8^2) = 2.5 × (5.76 - 3.24) = 6.3 W. 6.3 W is greater than 5.4 W.
